summaries.Good news: Today's uplifting stories show humanity actively solving problems: Chinese scientists cut oil refining energy use by 90%, students invented a 60-second concussion screener, and Australia's deserts could power a hydrogen revolution. Real breakthroughs that matter.
summaries.Ideas: Leadership and culture are shifting: Martha Stewart brings human expertise to the AI age, hobbies prove essential to success, and companies are reckoning with trust gaps and the human costs of workplace change. The conversation is moving beyond hype to what actually works.
summaries.Technology: From hybrid cargo ships cutting maritime emissions to miniature underwater drones and AI-powered music creation, breakthrough innovations are getting quieter, smaller, and more specialized—solving real problems rather than chasing hype.
summaries.Design: Design is exploring extremes: charred timber retreats for contemplation, nature-inspired climate-responsive architecture, and bold color expansion signal a shift toward both minimalism and maximalism as responses to contemporary life.

items.title: Chinese Scientists Develop New Oil Refining Method That Cuts Energy Use by 90%
items.snippet: Rather than bringing crude oil to boiling point over and over again as is done in traditional distillation refining, Chinese scientists have found a way to separate the mixture molecule by molecule at room temperature, cutting energy use by 90%. The groundbreaking discovery was done in the lab, and
items.line: A 90% reduction in energy use for oil refining using room-temperature molecular separation could reshape industrial energy consumption globally.

items.title: Students Win James Dyson Award for Device That Screens Students for Concussions in Just 60 Seconds
items.snippet: A trio of students at Harvard University have invented a low-cost, eye-tracking headset designed to help schools quickly screen child athletes for possible concussions. The invention takes just 2 to 3 minutes to screen for a concussion, or at least indicate sub-concussive trauma may be present, and
items.line: Harvard students' eye-tracking concussion screener delivers medical-grade diagnostics in 60 seconds, democratizing athlete safety across resource-constrained schools.
